c1-m1.summary: The user is feeling stressed and experiencing a challenging situation with their work and personal life.
c1-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm feeling a bit stressed out lately. Do you have any suggestions on how to manage stress?
Assistant: I'm so sorry to hear that you're feeling stressed. There are many ways to manage stress, but it would be helpful to know what's causing it. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
User: Well, I've just been having a lot on my plate lately. Work has been keeping me busy, and I've also been trying to take care of some personal things.
Assistant: It sounds like you have a lot of responsibilities. Are you finding it difficult to balance your work and personal life?
User: Yeah, that's exactly it. I feel like I'm being pulled in too many different directions. And to make matters worse, I have a big commitment coming up that I'm worried about.
Assistant: I see. It can be overwhelming when you have a lot of commitments to juggle. Can you tell me more about this big commitment that's coming up?
User: Well...I think I'll just say that it involves taking care of someone. And I'm not sure if I'll be able to do it on my own.
Assistant: Taking care of someone can be a big responsibility. Is this someone who is dependent on you, like a child or an elderly family member?
User: Yeah...it's a child, actually. I need to make sure they're taken care of, but I'm not sure if I'll be able to do it myself.
Assistant: That can be a big challenge. Have you considered getting some help with childcare? Maybe a babysitter or a nanny?
User: Actually, that's exactly what I'm looking for. A reliable babysitter would be a huge help right now. Do you have any suggestions on how to find one?
Assistant: There are many ways to find a reliable babysitter. You could ask friends or family members for recommendations, or look for local babysitting services in your area. You could also try searching online for babysitters in your area.
User: That's a great idea. What are some things I should look for when interviewing potential babysitters?
Assistant: When interviewing potential babysitters, you'll want to ask them about their experience working with children, their availability, and their approach to childcare. You should also ask for references and make sure they have any necessary certifications, such as CPR or first aid training.
User: Okay, that's really helpful. And what about background checks? Should I be doing those too?
Assistant: Yes, it's a good idea to do a background check on any potential babysitter. This can give you peace of mind and help ensure the safety of the child. There are many services that offer background checks, or you can ask the babysitter to provide one themselves.
User: Hi, I'm looking for some advice on job searching. Do you have any tips?
Assistant: Yes, I can provide you with some general tips. Networking is a great way to start, as many jobs are found through referrals. It's also essential to tailor your resume and cover letter to the specific job you're applying for. What kind of job are you looking for?
User: I'm looking for a job in marketing. I've been applying to many positions, but I haven't had much luck.
Assistant: Marketing is a competitive field. Have you considered reaching out to people in your industry for advice or informational interviews? This can be a great way to learn more about the field and make connections.
User: That's a great idea. However, I'm not sure where to start. I don't know many people in the marketing industry.
Assistant: You can start by attending industry events or joining online groups and forums related to marketing. This can be a great way to meet people and make connections. You can also try reaching out to alumni from your university or colleagues of friends who work in the industry.
User: I've tried attending some events, but I haven't had much success in making meaningful connections. I feel like everyone already knows each other, and it's hard to break in.
Assistant: It can be challenging to make connections at events, especially if you're introverted or new to the industry. Another approach is to ask friends and family members if they know anyone in the marketing industry who might be willing to chat with you.
User: That's the thing – my social circle is small, limiting my ability to get referrals from trusted friends and family members. I feel like I'm at a disadvantage compared to others who have a larger network.
Assistant: Having a small social circle can make it more challenging to get referrals. However, it's not impossible. You can try joining online communities or groups related to marketing, where you can connect with others who share similar interests. You can also consider volunteering for a cause you care about, which can be a great way to meet like-minded people.
User: I haven't thought of volunteering. How can that help me meet people in the marketing industry?
Assistant: Volunteering for a cause you care about can be a great way to meet people who share similar interests and values. Even if the people you meet aren't directly in the marketing industry, they may know someone who is. Additionally, volunteering can be a great way to build your skills and experience, which can be attractive to potential employers.
User: That makes sense. Do you have any tips on how to approach people I meet while volunteering?
Assistant: When approaching people you meet while volunteering, be genuine and authentic. Don't try to sell yourself or ask for a job on the spot. Instead, focus on building a relationship and learning more about the other person. Ask them about their interests and experiences, and see if you have any common connections.
User: Okay, I think I can try that. What about online communities? Are there any specific platforms or groups you recommend?
Assistant: There are many online communities related to marketing that you can join. Some popular platforms include LinkedIn groups, Reddit forums, and Facebook groups. Look for groups that align with your interests and goals, and participate in discussions to build your reputation and connect with others.
User: Alright, I'll check those out. Thanks for your advice!
Assistant: You're welcome! Remember, building a network takes time and effort. Don't get discouraged if it doesn't happen overnight. Keep working at it, and eventually, you'll make meaningful connections that can help you in your job search.

c3-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hey, I'm thinking of doing some home renovations. What are some popular projects that people usually start with?
Assistant: That's exciting! There are many great projects to start with, but it really depends on your priorities and needs. Some popular ones include upgrading the kitchen, adding a backyard patio, or creating a home office. What's been on your mind lately?
User: Actually, I've been thinking about the kids a lot. They're growing up so fast, and I want to make sure our home is safe and comfortable for them.
Assistant: That's completely understandable! As a parent, it's natural to want the best for your little ones. Have you considered any specific changes or upgrades that would make your home more kid-friendly?
User: Not yet, but I'm open to suggestions. What are some common things that parents do to make their homes more suitable for young children?
Assistant: Well, some popular options include installing safety gates, securing heavy furniture, and creating a play area with soft flooring. But it really depends on the age and needs of your kids. Can you tell me a bit more about them?
User: They're still pretty young, so they need constant supervision. Sometimes it's hard to keep an eye on them when I'm in another room.
Assistant: I can imagine! It can be challenging to balance keeping an eye on them while also getting things done around the house. Have you thought about using any technology to help with that?
User: Actually, I've been considering installing security cameras in the nursery and play areas to monitor the kids remotely. But I'm not sure where to start or what kind of cameras would be best.
Assistant: That's a great idea! Security cameras can give you peace of mind and allow you to keep an eye on the kids from another room. When it comes to choosing cameras, there are a few things to consider. Do you want wired or wireless cameras? And do you need any special features, like night vision or motion detection?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I think wireless cameras would be easier to install, but I'm not sure about the special features. What do you recommend?
Assistant: Well, night vision can be useful if you want to be able to see the kids at night, and motion detection can alert you if something unusual is happening. But it really depends on your specific needs and concerns. Why don't I give you a few recommendations, and you can do some research to see what works best for you?
User: That sounds great, thank you! I really appreciate your help.
Assistant: You're welcome! It's my pleasure to assist you. Remember to also consider the placement of the cameras and make sure they're securely installed to avoid any accidents. If you have any more questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

c13-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Given the text: Four days ago, I hid a small tape recorder in a bookcase at about five minutes before the hour when our sitter was due to arrive. His name is Justin, and he is a student at the university where I myself am working toward an advanced degree. He is friendly, likeable. Little clouds of sparse beard appear at his jaw, above a choker of painted red beads. From wide-spaced eyes the color of tea comes a warm and steady light.
I have nothing against Justin. A responsible father, however, must ask: what leads a boy of his age to want to sit for a six-month-old girl?
"Good money," was the response of my wife, Sherrene. "Same reason the others called."
"The others were girls," I said.
"Were they girls?" she sang, nose to nose with our daughter, Josie, who produced bubbling laughs. "Were the other ones girls?"
It was not yet dawn. Sherrene was dressing for work. She had slipped on a skirt and blue hose that had gone transparent at the heel and sole. In order to reach Josie, whom we had propped up in our bed, she'd let herself fall and bounce.
I was still in my nightclothes, a T-shirt and boxer shorts. I was standing. I said, "Why not a girl?"
As Sherrene rose and then frowned into the mirror at her dresser in order to brush out her hair, our daughter began fussing.
"Did you not say you thought I should make the decision?"
"I called all of his references. Two separate people said to me, Justin, he's wonderful, he's part of the family. Justin, we love him."
Hoisting our daughter up into my arms, I said, "Hey. It's your Daddy. Don't cry."
"I wasn't looking for a guy sitter."
I said, "Why do you cry with me, Josie?" I said, "I think she wants you."
This was a week ago, maybe three days before I hid the recorder behind a half-row of books.
I've been listening to the tape. Much of it sounds exactly how one might expect—accidental. A faraway drawer will slide open. A toy will beep a few bars of a waltz. Then nothing. Things stir but recede immediately into the faint gush of passing time.
But a portion of the tape has drawn my attention. I've transferred it onto my laptop, where it can be played as a continuous loop.
She is laughing, Josie, and continuing to laugh. When she breathes, another sound can be heard, much lower—the laughter of Justin.
In all of the ways I have pictured the scene, there is no cause to fear for her welfare. Still I replay it. After Sherrene has kissed me goodnight, I reach for the laptop, lower the sound, and open the audio file, which I have given the name "clip2."
Josie laughs, then doesn't, then does. It is like a tiny, bouncing wheel. At points it slows down, and the broader of the two laughs seems to rise, Justin's. His is steady, unpunctuated. It escapes him as freely as breath.
I try to be a good person. Honest, considerate. I try to work hard, so I can finish this degree, so I can start earning money, so we can be more secure.
I try to be who I should be, for Sherrene, for our family.
The question, adrift in the midnight stillness, ineluctable: have I failed?

User: Here is a piece of text: Making sure you're still connecting as a couple always makes for a better, more relaxing trip.
Published March 10, 2018 at 1:06 p.m.
My husband and I love to travel – with AND without our kids (read my post about why I believe parents should travel without kids too). When we are traveling with our family of five and also with friends and/or extended family, we've learned that there are a few things we always try to do to touch base with each other throughout the trip.
Making sure we're still connecting as a couple always makes for a better, more relaxing trip. Travel with kids is not always easy (but ALWAYS worth it, in our opinion) and connecting with your spouse while traveling helps elevate the fun and also alleviate some of the hard.
Below are my five best tips for staying connected with your spouse or partner when traveling with kids. Some of these tips are obvious and some we've learned through trial and error, no doubt!
My husband and I make a point to have some discussion time – alone – to process the day and sometimes talk about the day ahead. We do this on a daily basis, but especially when traveling with kids.
Brad and I usually do this in bed at night after we've put the girls down or in the morning when we're awake and alone in our room. We briefly talk through the day – things we struggled with or something we noticed about the kids or the day that was magical or just cool. Even if was a tough and exhausting day, briefly talking through the day with him always helps me to appreciate it more … and also discuss how to adjust things if needed.
On earlier trips as a family when we didn't do this, we often ended up having a lot of miscommunications and little things become big blown up things – while the small magical moments got overlooked.
Sometimes when traveling with kids, friends or extended family, we forget to hold hands while we're busy wrangling kids or hug when we need one. Brad is actually really good at grabbing me for a hug or quietly putting his hand on my knee at moments when we're traveling, and it instantly calms and relaxes me.
On our most recent trip, friends we were visiting offered to watch our kids while we had a night out – it was heaven. Sometimes we try to reciprocate this for other families. Often, my mom will do this when we visit her or my in-laws will watch all the cousins so that we can go out with my husband's brothers and spouses. At the beach, we may have an older cousin hang out with the kids while we take a walk or even just run to the grocery store together. I have friends who often find a babysitter in the city they are visiting – or talk to the hotel concierge or Airbnb host for recommendations. While date nights are admittedly rare (for us) when traveling with kids, I believe you should take advantage of them when you can!
My husband and I are both introverts and need a good dose of alone time to refuel. He is a very early riser – even on vacation – so he typically gets his in the morning. But occasionally, I can tell that he needs some quiet time while we're traveling and I make it a point to do something with the girls or send him out on a fun errand (coffee?). He's also very aware when I need my time and he'll take the kids out on an adventure so that I can read or nap or even simply take a walk on my own.
We laugh a lot when we travel. We laugh at our mistakes and mishaps, we laugh in the evenings over a glass of wine while recalling said mishaps, we laugh at the girls' funny antics or our funny antics with the girls. One of my favorite things about our recent trip is how much we laughed – with friends, with the girls, with each other. I laughed to tears more times than I can count and I love that connection with my love.

My husband and I make a point to have some discussion time – alone – to process the day and sometimes talk about the day ahead. We do this on a daily basis, but especially when traveling with kids.

Brad is actually really good at grabbing me for a hug or quietly putting his hand on my knee at moments when we're traveling, and it instantly calms and relaxes me.
On our most recent trip, friends we were visiting offered to watch our kids while we had a night out – it was heaven. Sometimes we try to reciprocate this for other families. Often, my mom will do this when we visit her or my in-laws will watch all the cousins so that we can go out with my husband's brothers and spouses. At the beach, we may have an older cousin hang out with the kids while we take a walk or even just run to the grocery store together. I have friends who often find a babysitter in the city they are visiting – or talk to the hotel concierge or Airbnb host for recommendations. While date nights are admittedly rare (for us) when traveling with kids, I believe you should take advantage of them when you can!

But occasionally, I can tell that he needs some quiet time while we're traveling and I make it a point to do something with the girls or send him out on a fun errand (coffee?). He's also very aware when I need my time and he'll take the kids out on an adventure so that I can read or nap or even simply take a walk on my own.
We laugh a lot when we travel. We laugh at our mistakes and mishaps, we laugh in the evenings over a glass of wine while recalling said mishaps, we laugh at the girls' funny antics or our funny antics with the girls. One of my favorite things about our recent trip is how much we laughed – with friends, with the girls, with each other. I laughed to tears more times than I can count and I love that connection with my love.

User: Evaluate the use of CGI in the action scenes of a recent science fiction movie and describe how it enhances or detracts from the viewing experience.
Assistant: I do not have the capability to watch movies, but I can provide a general description of how cgi (computer-generated imagery) affects action scenes in science fiction movies.

cgi is commonly used in action scenes in science fiction movies to create visually stunning and realistic special effects. With cgi, filmmakers can create scenes that would otherwise be impossible to achieve using traditional practical effects. For example, cgi can be used to generate realistic-looking alien creatures, massive explosions, and elaborate space battles, which would be difficult and expensive to create using traditional techniques.

the use of cgi in action scenes is generally considered to enhance the viewing experience for audiences. When used effectively, cgi can create a sense of immersion and excitement for viewers, making them feel like they are part of the action. It can also help to elevate the overall production value of a movie and make it more visually appealing.

however, the excessive use of cgi can detract from the viewing experience. When cgi is used carelessly or excessively, it can create a sense of artificiality and remove the viewer from the immersion in the movie. Additionally, poorly executed cgi can make the scenes disjointed and difficult to follow.

in summary, the use of cgi in action scenes in science fiction movies can enhance the viewing experience when used appropriately. The key is to strike a balance between using cgi to create visually stunning effects while still maintaining a sense of realism and believability.
User: Interesting! Can you provide some examples of recent science fiction movies that had great use of CGI in their action scenes? Also, could you provide more information on the impact of poorly executed CGI on a movie's viewing experience?
Assistant: Certainly! Some examples of recent science fiction movies that had great use of CGI in their action scenes include:

- Avengers: Endgame: This film used CGI extensively to create epic superhero battles and make characters appear giant or small. The CGI was executed seamlessly and made the action scenes thrilling and immersive.

- Ready Player One: This film used CGI to create a futuristic virtual world with stunning visuals and dynamic action scenes. The CGI was crucial to creating the film's immersive and hyper-realistic atmosphere.

- Blade Runner 2049: This film used CGI to create a dystopian, futuristic world with stunning visuals and realistic effects. The CGI complemented the film's dark, moody atmosphere and made the action scenes more intense and immersive.

Poorly executed CGI can have a significant impact on a movie's viewing experience. When CGI fails to convincingly create realistic creatures or environments, it can reduce the film's immersion and feel artificial or cartoonish. Moreover, poorly executed CGI can distract the audience and take them out of the film's story.

For example, the 2019 movie, "Cats" used CGI to create realistic-looking anthropomorphic cats, but the final result was widely panned by critics and audiences for being awkward and unsettling. The poor execution of CGI in "Cats" detracted from the overall enjoyment of the film and led to negative reviews and criticism.
User: Thanks for the great examples! Can you provide me with more information on how CGI is created and integrated into a movie's action scenes?
Assistant: Certainly! The process of creating and integrating CGI into a movie's action scenes typically involves several steps:

1. Pre-visualization (Pre-viz): The filmmaker works with a team of animators to create a rough version of the planned action scenes using 3D models and computer-generated storyboards. These pre-viz representations are used to explore various camera angles, timings, and effects that will be used in the final version of the scene.

2. Modeling: Once the pre-viz is approved, the animators then create detailed 3D models of the characters, creatures, or objects that will appear in the scene. These models are typically built using specialized software and can take anywhere from a few days to several months to create.

3. Animation: Once the 3D models are created, animators use various software to animate them to create movement and action that matches the pre-viz. Motion capture technology may be used to record actors' movements and then apply them to the 3D characters.

4. Rendering: After the animation is completed, the entire scene is rendered, or processed, in multiple layers to add the lighting, texture, and special effects necessary to make it look realistic.

5. Integration: Finally, the rendered scene is integrated into the live-action footage. They must be color-corrected, have their shadows and reflections match reality, and must be synchronized with sound effects and other audio. 

The process of creating and integrating CGI can be quite complex and time-consuming but when executed effectively, it can enhance a movie's action scenes greatly.

2. SideFX Houdini: This is a 3D animation and visual effects software used for creating complex simulations, such as explosions, fires, and simulations of fluids, and particles.

3. Maxon Cinema 4D: This is a 3D modeling, animation, and motion graphics software that is often used by industry professionals in the film, TV, and advertising industries.

4. Adobe After Effects: This is a visual effects and motion graphics software that is often used to create detailed composites of live-action footage and CGI.

5. Nuke: Nuke is a node-based digital compositing software that is often used for high-end visual effects in film and television.

These software programs are very powerful, and many of them require significant expertise and training to use effectively. In addition to these standard programs, film studios may also use bespoke software and tools designed specifically for their pipeline and production pipeline.

The choice of a particular software depends on the requirements of the project and the skillset of the filmmakers involved.

Passage: When the workday, better yet the workweek, is done, most of us want to get away from it all, even if only for a couple of hours. The most popular method of escaping from reality is entertainment. But most of it is so darn expensive. Of the big four diversions: Sports events, live theater, live music, and movies, that last one is still the biggest bargain. Yet the price of admission keeps going up. According to the National Association of Theatre Owners, in 2015, an average movie ticket was $8.25; in 2016, $8.65; last year, $8.97. In 2018, it’ll cost you an average of $9.16 to see your favorite star or franchise.
With the summertime onslaught of all sorts of movies about to hit us, there’s a need for some guidance, some way to figure out where you might get the biggest bang for your buck. After going through seemingly endless lists of releases scheduled between mid-May and August, here are the top 10 suggestions of films that should engage you and make you happy you saw them, no matter what the cost.
May 18: “Deadpool 2” — Former fast-talking mercenary Wade Wilson AKA Deadpool (Ryan Reynolds) is back, trying out a new career as a bartender — and travelling through time. The villain is mean-spirited Cable (Josh Brolin).
May 25: “Solo: A Star Wars Story” — Long before “a long time ago,” young Han Solo (Alden Ehrenreich) met young Chewbacca (Joonas Suotamo) and young Lando Calrissian (Donald Glover). Intergalactic adventures ensued.
June 8: “Ocean’s 8” — Danny Ocean’s sister Debbie (Sandra Bullock) gets together a gang of gals — Cate Blanchett, Anne Hathaway, and Helena Bonham Carter among them — to pull off a big New York heist.
June 15: “The Incredibles 2” — Pixar and the Parr family are back, but Mr. Incredible has become a homebody while Elastigirl is out saving the world. Here’s hoping that Frozone can find his super suit.
June 22: “Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom” — There are still plenty of dinosaurs on that island, but when a volcano threatens their existence, our human heroes — Chris Pratt, Bryce Dallas Howard and, returning to the franchise, Jeff Goldblum — try to save them.
July 6: “Ant-Man and The Wasp” — Ant-Man (Paul Rudd) attempts to keep professional and personal lives in balance when he’s asked to team up with the Wasp (Evangeline Lilly) under the guidance of mentor Dr. Hank Pym (Michael Douglas).
July 13: “Skyscraper” — Massive-armed Dwayne Johnson is the security expert and hero who’s framed for a fire in a skyscraper, then must find the real culprits.
July 27: “Mission: Impossible — Fallout” — Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and some cohorts must make things right on a mission that, while not exactly impossible, has gone very wrong.
Aug. 3: “Christopher Robin” — Mixing live action with CGI, the adult Christopher Robin (Ewan McGregor) reunites with his old pal Winnie the Pooh with hopes of finding Pooh’s missing friends.
Aug. 17: “The Happytime Murders” — It’s a Muppet noir, in which puppet cast-members of a kiddie TV show are being bumped off, and a private detective puppet attempts to solve the crimes.

User: When my young love-life reached the point of aimlessness and more serious unanswered questions about life had arised, one answer was already there and definite: I never wanted to be a film critic!
Everytime when I scrolled through a newspaper or magazine and a critique appeared, I thought to myself: Why would anybody want to read this? The most common answer by relatives and friends was: "People read this because they want to know whether they should go see the movie or not."
Nowadays there are many critiques like this in the newspapers and all over the internet: Three point five out of five stars, "Exceptional", "Recommended before or after candle-light dinner" and if you are honest the accompanying ten lines of text are rarely more revealing than a trailer or a poster. Therefore I don´t consider "Go / Don´t go!"-critiques as critiques but as almost useless information.
The more sophisticated answer to my question is "It´s a judgement of the movie by a film critic".
The modern trend in film critiques goes something like this: The film is the object. The critic who watched the film is not the subject. The critic is objective! How can he? Well, he is a film critic. He does not care if you are going to watch the film or not. He believes that after you read his critique you know everything about the film and especially it´s impact on our universe. He tells you what actors are "good" in the film, whether the director "succeeded" or not and so on. He makes you forget that he in fact is nothing more than a Pete with a pen and since we don´t know anything about Pete and his personal life, his critique is as worthless as a lamp without a bulb.
You might have noticed that the reason why you go to the movies is everything else but a film critic or his review. Most of the time it is a friend telling you that you "must see it!". And rarely more. And you go there!
b) friends who all read the same magazine.
But this is not important and who cares for them anyway? There must be a reason why they have no friends, right?
You might probably also have noticed, that you learn more about a friend of yours when you tell him about a film which you think is great and he tells you he thinks its crap. The arising discussion about the film usually fades into a discussion about personal likes and dislikes, art and beauty in general and often even about philosophical views on life.
Films are subjective statements. There is one film and many viewers. They see it and in them the film transforms into a new subjective statement. When somebody is talking about a film both of the following can happen: He reveals something about the film or the film reveals something about him. This happens in the same way in which the film reveals something about its director, as the film is the directors "critique or review" of a story or event that existed before his film (as a real event, a screenplay, an idea...). When we are talking about films we all transform into newly influenced different subjective statements about a film and sometimes, after a year or two we see the film again and notice - how much we have changed!
To that power of art in films I dedicate this blog. You will read my very subjective thoughts and impressions on newly released films and those that existed before I was born. You will read my rant and praise on others impressions. One thing I promise: It won´t be boring unless you are.

User: When my young love-life reached the point of aimlessness and more serious unanswered questions about life had arised, one answer was already there and definite: I never wanted to be a film critic!
Everytime when I scrolled through a newspaper or magazine and a critique appeared, I thought to myself: Why would anybody want to read this? The most common answer by relatives and friends was: "People read this because they want to know whether they should go see the movie or not."
Nowadays there are many critiques like this in the newspapers and all over the internet: Three point five out of five stars, "Exceptional", "Recommended before or after candle-light dinner" and if you are honest the accompanying ten lines of text are rarely more revealing than a trailer or a poster. Therefore I don´t consider "Go / Don´t go!"-critiques as critiques but as almost useless information.
The more sophisticated answer to my question is "It´s a judgement of the movie by a film critic".
The modern trend in film critiques goes something like this: The film is the object. The critic who watched the film is not the subject. The critic is objective! How can he? Well, he is a film critic. He does not care if you are going to watch the film or not. He believes that after you read his critique you know everything about the film and especially it´s impact on our universe. He tells you what actors are "good" in the film, whether the director "succeeded" or not and so on. He makes you forget that he in fact is nothing more than a Pete with a pen and since we don´t know anything about Pete and his personal life, his critique is as worthless as a lamp without a bulb.
You might have noticed that the reason why you go to the movies is everything else but a film critic or his review. Most of the time it is a friend telling you that you "must see it!". And rarely more. And you go there!
b) friends who all read the same magazine.
But this is not important and who cares for them anyway? There must be a reason why they have no friends, right?
You might probably also have noticed, that you learn more about a friend of yours when you tell him about a film which you think is great and he tells you he thinks its crap. The arising discussion about the film usually fades into a discussion about personal likes and dislikes, art and beauty in general and often even about philosophical views on life.
Films are subjective statements. There is one film and many viewers. They see it and in them the film transforms into a new subjective statement. When somebody is talking about a film both of the following can happen: He reveals something about the film or the film reveals something about him. This happens in the same way in which the film reveals something about its director, as the film is the directors "critique or review" of a story or event that existed before his film (as a real event, a screenplay, an idea...). When we are talking about films we all transform into newly influenced different subjective statements about a film and sometimes, after a year or two we see the film again and notice - how much we have changed!
To that power of art in films I dedicate this blog. You will read my very subjective thoughts and impressions on newly released films and those that existed before I was born. You will read my rant and praise on others impressions. One thing I promise: It won´t be boring unless you are.

Our favorite: this black and white sherpa detailed long coat.

Kate (Reese Witherspoon) may be mourning the fact she has to spend Christmas with four different families instead of on a tropical vacation - hence the all-black outfit - but she looks impossibly chic throughout the entire day, and somehow manages to stand in her Louboutins for a full 24 hours. Now that’s inspiring.
This classic is a must-watch every holiday season!
We forever adore Mary's (Donna Reed) feminine look here, a full-skirted dress with elegant embroidery around the neckline and hem complete with a timeless pearl necklace. It's the look that stole George (Jimmy Stewart) away!

Here girl-next-door baker Stacy De Nevo (Vanessa Hudgens) gets to play princess for the day by pretending to be look-alike royal Lady Margaret Delacourt (also Vanessa Hudgens) who wants to spend a couple days as a normal girl. User: Here is a piece of text: Mumbai: Hyderabad will host the first leg of season 3 of the Star Sports Pro Kabaddi League from January 30 next year, with the home team Telugu Titans taking on title holders U Mumba to kick-start the tournament at the Titans' home turf, Gachibowli Indoor Stadium. After the end of the two-part league stage, separated by one day's break, the play-off games would be held in New Delhi between March 4 and 6, according to a media release from the organisers yesterday.
PKL, organised by Mashal Sports and Star India, in association with the International Kabaddi Federation, Asian Kabaddi Federation and the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India, is now going to be a bi-annual league with two seasons every year, the release said. Season 3 is being held just five months after completion of the second season and would feature 60 games across 34 days in eight cities and following the same 'caravan style' format like in the first two seasons.
The League would be held at each franchise city for a duration of four days, where the home team would play four of the visiting franchises and all seven visiting franchises would play a set of away games in each city. After the opening leg in Hyderabad, the caravan would move to the Kanteerava Indoor Stadium, Bengaluru, to be followed by Netaji Indoor Stadium in Kolkata.
This season, the badminton arena in the Balewadi Sports Complex, Pune would be the venue for the culmination to the first half of the league. The indoor stadium at the Patliputra Sports Complex, Patna is the venue of the second half of the league with the caravan then moving to Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur on February 20.
Moving on from Jaipur, the league will be played in at the Thyagaraj Indoor Stadium in New Delhi and move to the home of the reigning champions at the National Sports Club of India, here. The play-offs would be held in the national capital for the semi-finals (March 4), 3-4 play-off game and the final (March 5/6), the release stated.

User: It is hard to forget the photograph that first brought Afshan Ashiq to the public eye. Dressed in a blue shalwar kameez, her face covered in a balaclava fashioned out of her dupatta, her body contorted as she hurls a rock at local security personnel, just out of frame. It bears almost no resemblance to the picture the 24-year-old cuts today as the goalkeeper for the Mumbai-based Premier India Football Academy and one of the best sporting talents to come out of Jammu & Kashmir in recent years.
The beautiful game has the potential to change Jammu & Kashmir same as it changed her life, Ashiq says. Always more popular than cricket, now football is enjoying a moment with stars such as Ashiq and the state’s first I-League football club, the Real Kashmir Football Club. “I still remember my first match at the club,” says Danish Farooq, who plays midfield. “We walked out on to the pitch with the crowds cheering us on. It was like being transported to a whole other world.” The club, formed just two years ago, has already managed to break into the country’s top-level football league playing against long-established competitors such as Mohun Bagan AC and East Bengal FC.

Called “Real” Kashmir, this series shows a version of the state’s reality that doesn’t often make it to the evening news.
And while the state still lacks the infrastructure to harness this passion for the sport, ambassadors like Ashiq are moving the needle. She met with the Chief Minister of the state and also petitioned the Home Minister to gain support for football. The result is there is now a State Football Academy funded by the local government and camps all around Jammu and Kashmir to develop sporting talent.

User: I will soon be completing my two years living in this great city of Mumbai. The home of Bollywood, glamour, and all things filmy! Being a big movie buff and a management student, I have always taken a keen interest in movies coming up in the theatres and how are they being publicized, promoted and advertised in and around the city where almost everything reeks of Bollywood. So let’s walk you through some of the things I have seen and experienced.
Billboards have always been the most popular way to grab attention. Towards the end of the last year, I woke up every morning to a cop-dressed goggle-eyed moustached Salman Khan staring at me from the big billboard right out there on the main road across my window, telling me to go and watch the sequel to his previous blockbuster film. Even though I haven’t watched it yet, looking at the box office numbers it raked up, I’m sure plenty of Indians have. The number of billboards in Mumbai which are specifically for film promotions, Bollywood and Hollywood both, were much more than what I had seen in any other city in the nation. Had to be I guess- this is the home of Bollywood. Starting from larger-than-life billboards to the smaller back-lit ones at the streetlight poles on the roads, it’s all around within punching distance of each other.
A recent Times Square like- innovation which I came across at the crossing in the up-market Juhu area is a video billboard – a giant digital screen which showed video trailers of the latest movies and other advertisements. A stylish and efficient way to showcase the different upcoming films I must say – especially to the people stuck in traffic (and trust me, traffic jams are quite an occurrence in the streets of Mumbai).
Let’s come to buses. The big red BEST buses of Mumbai. Often, I have failed to notice the bus number because I have been taken in more by the posters running across the entire body of the bus. The posters have Sanjay Dutt brandishing a pistol and pointing it at Arshad Warsi or Shahid Kapoor flashing a smile and trying to woo Priyanka Chopra – making the people out there travelling or standing on the streets aware of the latest movies in tinsel town and when they are going to hit the screens . This, to me, is an excellent way to advertise. Let’s say the bus starts from Goregaon and goes upto Worli, traversing the length of the city and areas in between – thus, unlike a billboard , it is not fixed to one location but on the move, catching the eyes and reaching out to a large number of people in different parts of the city everyday . The local trains are no exception and have also become such a medium of advertising.
Outdoor promotional campaigns done by the film houses with their star-cast are pretty common for the big-budget films. Malls, colleges and other public events are popular spots to do so. I happen to be studying on one of those campuses in Mumbai which are often frequented by movie stars and directors to promote their latest films. The young hip crowd present here, build up in large numbers amidst the euphoria of coming within ‘touching’ distance of their favorite movie stars.
This may not be exactly promotional, but I came across an interesting technological innovation at one of the multiplexes in the city. Just outside their ticket counters, there were three 42” television-sized touch screen panels which showed the different movies that were being screened along with their timings and the best part was: you can click on the movies, know a brief storyline about it, their cast and you can also watch the trailers. A nice way to decide which movie you should watch or just skip!
Well, movies and their promotional techniques are constantly evolving and with the advancement in technology, it is only going to get bigger and better. I only wish the billboard across my window puts up my favorite actresses flashing beautiful smiles , I’m tired of seeing brawny actors looking menacingly at me !

Let’s come to buses. The big red BEST buses of Mumbai. Often, I have failed to notice the bus number because I have been taken in more by the posters running across the entire body of the bus. The posters have Sanjay Dutt brandishing a pistol and pointing it at Arshad Warsi or Shahid Kapoor flashing a smile and trying to woo Priyanka Chopra – making the people out there travelling or standing on the streets aware of the latest movies in tinsel town and when they are going to hit the screens . This, to me, is an excellent way to advertise. Let’s say the bus starts from Goregaon and goes upto Worli, traversing the length of the city and areas in between – thus, unlike a billboard , it is not fixed to one location but on the move, catching the eyes and reaching out to a large number of people in different parts of the city everyday . The local trains are no exception and have also become such a medium of advertising.
Outdoor promotional campaigns done by the film houses with their star-cast are pretty common for the big-budget films. Malls, colleges and other public events are popular spots to do so. I happen to be studying on one of those campuses in Mumbai which are often frequented by movie stars and directors to promote their latest films. The young hip crowd present here, build up in large numbers amidst the euphoria of coming within ‘touching’ distance of their favorite movie stars.
This may not be exactly promotional, but I came across an interesting technological innovation at one of the multiplexes in the city. Just outside their ticket counters, there were three 42” television-sized touch screen panels which showed the different movies that were being screened along with their timings and the best part was: you can click on the movies, know a brief storyline about it, their cast and you can also watch the trailers. A nice way to decide which movie you should watch or just skip!
Well, movies and their promotional techniques are constantly evolving and with the advancement in technology, it is only going to get bigger and better. I only wish the billboard across my window puts up my favorite actresses flashing beautiful smiles , I’m tired of seeing brawny actors looking menacingly at me !

User: Here is a piece of text: Mumbai: Hyderabad will host the first leg of season 3 of the Star Sports Pro Kabaddi League from January 30 next year, with the home team Telugu Titans taking on title holders U Mumba to kick-start the tournament at the Titans' home turf, Gachibowli Indoor Stadium. After the end of the two-part league stage, separated by one day's break, the play-off games would be held in New Delhi between March 4 and 6, according to a media release from the organisers yesterday.
PKL, organised by Mashal Sports and Star India, in association with the International Kabaddi Federation, Asian Kabaddi Federation and the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India, is now going to be a bi-annual league with two seasons every year, the release said. Season 3 is being held just five months after completion of the second season and would feature 60 games across 34 days in eight cities and following the same 'caravan style' format like in the first two seasons.
The League would be held at each franchise city for a duration of four days, where the home team would play four of the visiting franchises and all seven visiting franchises would play a set of away games in each city. After the opening leg in Hyderabad, the caravan would move to the Kanteerava Indoor Stadium, Bengaluru, to be followed by Netaji Indoor Stadium in Kolkata.
This season, the badminton arena in the Balewadi Sports Complex, Pune would be the venue for the culmination to the first half of the league. The indoor stadium at the Patliputra Sports Complex, Patna is the venue of the second half of the league with the caravan then moving to Sawai Mansingh Stadium in Jaipur on February 20.
Moving on from Jaipur, the league will be played in at the Thyagaraj Indoor Stadium in New Delhi and move to the home of the reigning champions at the National Sports Club of India, here. The play-offs would be held in the national capital for the semi-finals (March 4), 3-4 play-off game and the final (March 5/6), the release stated.

User: I will soon be completing my two years living in this great city of Mumbai. The home of Bollywood, glamour, and all things filmy! Being a big movie buff and a management student, I have always taken a keen interest in movies coming up in the theatres and how are they being publicized, promoted and advertised in and around the city where almost everything reeks of Bollywood. So let’s walk you through some of the things I have seen and experienced.
Billboards have always been the most popular way to grab attention. Towards the end of the last year, I woke up every morning to a cop-dressed goggle-eyed moustached Salman Khan staring at me from the big billboard right out there on the main road across my window, telling me to go and watch the sequel to his previous blockbuster film. Even though I haven’t watched it yet, looking at the box office numbers it raked up, I’m sure plenty of Indians have. The number of billboards in Mumbai which are specifically for film promotions, Bollywood and Hollywood both, were much more than what I had seen in any other city in the nation. Had to be I guess- this is the home of Bollywood. Starting from larger-than-life billboards to the smaller back-lit ones at the streetlight poles on the roads, it’s all around within punching distance of each other.
A recent Times Square like- innovation which I came across at the crossing in the up-market Juhu area is a video billboard – a giant digital screen which showed video trailers of the latest movies and other advertisements. A stylish and efficient way to showcase the different upcoming films I must say – especially to the people stuck in traffic (and trust me, traffic jams are quite an occurrence in the streets of Mumbai).
Let’s come to buses. The big red BEST buses of Mumbai. Often, I have failed to notice the bus number because I have been taken in more by the posters running across the entire body of the bus. The posters have Sanjay Dutt brandishing a pistol and pointing it at Arshad Warsi or Shahid Kapoor flashing a smile and trying to woo Priyanka Chopra – making the people out there travelling or standing on the streets aware of the latest movies in tinsel town and when they are going to hit the screens . This, to me, is an excellent way to advertise. Let’s say the bus starts from Goregaon and goes upto Worli, traversing the length of the city and areas in between – thus, unlike a billboard , it is not fixed to one location but on the move, catching the eyes and reaching out to a large number of people in different parts of the city everyday . The local trains are no exception and have also become such a medium of advertising.
Outdoor promotional campaigns done by the film houses with their star-cast are pretty common for the big-budget films. Malls, colleges and other public events are popular spots to do so. I happen to be studying on one of those campuses in Mumbai which are often frequented by movie stars and directors to promote their latest films. The young hip crowd present here, build up in large numbers amidst the euphoria of coming within ‘touching’ distance of their favorite movie stars.
This may not be exactly promotional, but I came across an interesting technological innovation at one of the multiplexes in the city. Just outside their ticket counters, there were three 42” television-sized touch screen panels which showed the different movies that were being screened along with their timings and the best part was: you can click on the movies, know a brief storyline about it, their cast and you can also watch the trailers. A nice way to decide which movie you should watch or just skip!
Well, movies and their promotional techniques are constantly evolving and with the advancement in technology, it is only going to get bigger and better. I only wish the billboard across my window puts up my favorite actresses flashing beautiful smiles , I’m tired of seeing brawny actors looking menacingly at me !
